newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - API's seen neutral unless crude build high.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - API's seen neutral unless crude build high.

text.p: This week's report from the American Petroleum Institute (API) looks likely to be neutral with sundry seasonally changes, but all bets are off if a widely forecast crude build comes in high, traders said.
Industry sources expect the report to show higher crude stocks and refinery utilization rates, as well as lower gasoline and distillate (heating oil and diesel) stocks.
"The key feature will probably be crude. A build of over four million barrels will keep this market heading south," said Jim Ritterbusch, trader at Sweeney Oil in Chicago.
But most sources expect crude stocks to build by no more than three million barrels from the prior week level of 304.7 million barrels, with the average computed at 1.75 million.
Sources like Ritterbusch said they expected imports to remain at somewhat high levels over eight million barrels per day with refinery demand not high enough to offset the solid import levels.

But those bucking the predominant thinking, such as ING Derivatives' Tom Bentz, expect that crude imports will not be high enough to offset growing refinery run rates and, as a result, crude stocks could drop by as much as 3.5 million.

Most sources indeed saw refinery utilization rates rising by an average of 0.50 percentage point above the prior week level of 90.4 percent as the wintertime refinery maintenance season gives way to a seasonal rise in gasoline demand.

But some, like Refco's vice president of futures trading expect run rates to drop as a result of a number of refinery hiccups in the last week which he reckons could drag run rates down by as much as one percentage point.
Gasoline stocks were seen coming in unchanged to two million barrels below the 198.2 million level recorded in API's report last week.

"Any drop in gasoline should be considered bullish," said Thomas Blakeslee, analyst with Cargill Investor Services in New York, forecasting implied demand at 7.8 barrels per day against supply (output plus imports) of 7.6 million bpd.
Heating oil stocks were meanwhile expected to draw by over two million bpd from the prior week levels of 103.3 million just as NYMEX prices were leading the market upward Tuesday.
"The biggest plus for heating oil is that the winter's over," said one trader explaining heat's strength, and noting heat stocks are relatively irrelevant until late summer.
